'''Equitrans Gas Pipeline''' is an operating natural gas pipeline in the United States.<ref name="rce8fac">{{Cite web|url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/33213/000003321326000018/eqt-20251231.htm|title=EQT Corporation annual report on Form 10-K for 2025|website=sec.gov|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref><ref name="r2ed193">{{Cite web|url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1747009/000174700924000011/etrn-20231231.htm|title=Equitrans Midstream Corporation annual report on Form 10-K for 2023|website=sec.gov|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref>

==Location==
Equitrans Mainline: The pipeline runs from West Virginia to Pennsylvania.<ref name="r2c6622">{{Cite web|url=http://web.archive.org/web/20230610002101/https://www.ovcx.info/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/0012-PUBLIC-Exhibit-Z-3.pdf|title=Equitrans, L.P., Ohio Valley Connector Expansion Project, Exhibit Z-3, Open Season Notices|website=web.archive.org|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref><ref name="r2ed193" />
Equitrans Allenghy Valley Connector: The pipeline is located in Pennsylvania.<ref name="rc9ccee">{{Cite web|url=https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2015/10/08/2015-25635/equitrans-lp-notice-of-application|title=Equitrans, L.P.; Notice of Application, Federal Register, 8 October 2015|website=federalregister.gov|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref><ref name="re9bcd6">{{Cite web|url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/33213/000003321317000003/eqt-12312016x10k.htm|title=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/33213/000003321317000003/eqt-12312016x10k.htm|website=sec.gov|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref>
Ohio Valley Connector: The pipeline runs from West Virginia to Ohio.<ref name="r30800f">{{Cite web|url=https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjectsAug2026.xlsx|title=Natural Gas Pipeline Projects, U.S. Energy Information Administration, August 2026|website=eia.gov|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref><ref name="r09df77">{{Cite web|url=https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2014-09-08/html/2014-21206.htm|title=Equitrans, L.P.; Notice of Intent To Prepare an Environmental Assessment for the Planned Ohio Valley Connector Project, Federal Register, 8 September 2014|website=govinfo.gov|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref>
Sunrise Pipeline Project: The pipeline runs from Wetzel County, West Virginia to Greene County, Pennsylvania.<ref name="r1459f5">{{Cite web|url=https://regulations.justia.com/regulations/fedreg/2011/05/18/2011-12118.html|title=https://regulations.justia.com/regulations/fedreg/2011/05/18/2011-12118.html|website=regulations.justia.com|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref>

==Background==
===Equitrans Mainline===
A 2021 open season notice from Equitrans, L.P. described its Mainline system as a natural gas transmission and storage system in north central West Virginia, southwestern Pennsylvania, and eastern Ohio. Equitrans, L.P. is a subsidiary of Equitrans Midstream Corporation.<ref name="r2c6622" /> EQT Corporation acquired Equitrans Midstream in a merger, and EQT's results include the acquired assets from July 22, 2024.<ref name="rce8fac" />

The sources give figures for the whole transmission and storage system and not for the Mainline alone. As of December 31, 2022, the system included about 940 miles of interstate pipelines regulated by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. Its total throughput capacity was about 4.4 Bcf per day.<ref name="rbd5939" />

===Equitrans Allenghy Valley Connector===
EQT Midstream Partners announced on October 13, 2016 that it had acquired the Allegheny Valley Connector transmission and storage system from EQT Corporation for $275 million in cash. The acquisition was effective October 1, 2016.<ref name="ra976ef" /> The system includes about 209 miles of transmission pipeline and 11 Bcf of working gas storage capacity. It has 450 MMcf per day of transmission capacity.<ref name="ra976ef" /> The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission regulates it.<ref name="ra976ef" /> In September 2015 Equitrans asked the Commission to restate the certificated storage capacity of the system to 11.2 Bcf of working gas, down from 15.1 Bcf.<ref name="rc9ccee" />

A May 2019 notice described plans to replace about 3.85 miles of 20-inch pipe on the TP-4555 pipeline, which is part of the Allegheny Valley Connector System, with about 3.92 miles of new 20-inch pipe in Westmoreland County, Pennsylvania.<ref name="r42b3fe" /> In January 2026 Equitrans asked to abandon in place the West Fairfield Compressor Station. It said the station was no longer needed to meet its firm obligations on the system.<ref name="r03b514" />

===Ohio Valley Connector===
Equitrans, L.P. filed an application with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on December 30, 2014 to build the Ohio Valley Connector Project in West Virginia and Ohio. It proposed 50 miles of pipeline and 36,000 horsepower of compression. The project would provide up to 850,000 dekatherms per day of added firm transportation service. Equitrans estimated the cost at $416.00 million and proposed an in-service date of June 2016.<ref name="rf59d99" /> An earlier notice from September 2014 described 34 miles of 30-inch pipeline, 1.5 miles of 30-inch pipeline, and 14 miles of 24-inch loop.<ref name="r09df77" />

An October 2016 company release said the pipeline began transportation service on October 1, 2016 from northern West Virginia to Clarington, Ohio. It described the pipeline as a 37-mile extension. EQT held a 20-year agreement for 650 MMcf per day of firm capacity on it.<ref name="r06fd46" /> In January 2022 Equitrans applied for an Ohio Valley Connector Expansion Project to provide up to 350,000 dekatherms per day of added deliverability.<ref name="r09871f" /> Equitrans Midstream expected to spend about $40 million in 2024 to complete that expansion.<ref name="r2ed193" />

===Sunrise Pipeline Project===
Equitrans, L.P. proposed the Sunrise Pipeline Project in Federal Energy Regulatory Commission docket CP11-68. In a notice published May 18, 2011, FERC staff said the project would also include 2.6 miles of replacement pipe, the uprating of 4.8 miles of existing pipe, and a new compressor station in Jefferson Township, Greene County, Pennsylvania. It listed five meter station interconnects, 12 mainline block valves and four pig launchers and receivers. Comments on the environmental assessment were due June 10, 2011.<ref name="r1459f5" />

The U.S. Energy Information Administration lists the project as completed on July 19, 2012, at a cost of $272 million. It gives the length as 50 miles, while the 2011 notice gave 44.4 miles of new pipe.<ref name="r30800f" />
